does: Fries coated, filled rice balls a few at a time in hot oil deep enough to cover them, turning them until the shell is deep golden all round and the filling inside is hot and soft.
how: Heat plenty of oil in a deep, heavy pan and hold it steady. A crumb dropped in should sizzle at once and rise.
Lower a few balls in with a slotted spoon. Do not crowd the pan, or the oil cools and the shells go greasy.
Turn them gently until they are deep golden all round. Keep the heat moderate, so that the warmth reaches the filling before the shell gets too dark.
Lift them out onto a rack and let the oil run off. Rest them briefly before serving, because the middle stays very hot.

cues.text: A sharp, steady sizzle as they go in, which quietens as the shell sets.
An even deep gold all round, with no cracks in the shell.
A ball is light for its size and the shell feels firm and dry when pressed.

mistakes.mistake: Frying in oil that is too hot, so that the shell turns dark while the filling is still cold.
mistakes.fix: Keep the oil at a steady, moderate heat and use a thermometer.

mistakes.mistake: Frying in oil that is not hot enough, so that the shell soaks up oil and splits.
mistakes.fix: Wait until a crumb sizzles at once, and fry only a few at a time.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, which cools the oil.
mistakes.fix: Fry in small batches and let the oil heat up again between them.

comes_after.why: There is nothing to fry until the balls are shaped, coated and chilled.

variant_of.differs: The food is a filled ball of rice in a crumb shell, and the filling has to be hot all through when the shell is done, so the oil is held steady and moderate and only a few go in each time.
The balls are larger and hold a filling in a firm rice wall, and not a soft paste, so they stay in the oil a little longer at a slightly gentler heat for the middle to warm.
